body:
## Pull request overview

This PR realigns the documentation with the current 11‑namespace protocol architecture, replacing the older ObjectQL/ObjectOS/ObjectUI “Trinity” framing and adding dedicated concept pages for each protocol. It also updates English and Chinese architecture/terminology pages and restructures the concepts navigation to surface the new protocol docs.

**Changes:**
- Reframed the core architecture docs (EN/CN) around 11 protocol namespaces mapped to three layers (Data, Control, View) and added a protocol dependency overview.
- Updated ecosystem terminology (EN/CN) and enterprise-patterns docs to use the new protocol names (Data, Automation, Hub, etc.) instead of the legacy ObjectQL/ObjectOS/ObjectUI terms.
- Added detailed concept pages for each protocol namespace (Data, Driver, Permission, UI, System, Auth, Kernel, Hub, AI, API, Automation) and wired them into the concepts sidebar metadata (EN/CN).

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 19 out of 19 changed files in this pull request and generated 12 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| content/docs/concepts/terminology.mdx | Updates ecosystem terminology to describe the 11 protocol namespaces and aligns concept definitions (e.g., Virtual Field, Layout, Workflow) with the new Data/UI/Automation/Hub/Permission wording. |
| content/docs/concepts/terminology.cn.mdx | Chinese terminology page updated in parallel with the English version to reflect protocol namespaces and revised definitions. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-ui.mdx | New concept page documenting the UI Protocol, including apps, list/form views, dashboards, reports, actions, themes, and dynamic rendering examples. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-system.mdx | New System Protocol page covering event bus, job scheduler, translations, and audit logging, with example schemas for events, jobs, i18n bundles, and audit config. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-permission.mdx | New Permission Protocol page describing object permissions, FLS, OWD, sharing rules, territories, and evaluation flow, with high-level TypeScript examples. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-kernel.mdx | New Kernel Protocol page documenting manifest structure, plugin lifecycle, plugin context, logger configuration, and scoped storage concepts. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-hub.mdx | New Hub Protocol page for multi-tenancy, marketplace plugins, licensing, and deployment spaces, with example Hub.* configurations. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-driver.mdx | New Driver Protocol page covering driver interface, capabilities, built-in drivers, datasource configuration, custom driver implementation, and query compilation examples. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-data.mdx | New Data Protocol page outlining object schemas, field types, query AST, validation rules, and typical modelling patterns (master-detail, formula, rollup). |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-automation.mdx | New Automation Protocol page that introduces workflows, visual flows, and webhooks with illustrative Automation.* examples. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-auth.mdx | New Auth Protocol page defining identity, auth strategies, sessions, roles, organizations, and security policies with example Auth.* configs. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-api.mdx | New API Protocol concept page describing REST contracts, discovery, realtime subscriptions, and custom route definitions. |
| content/docs/concepts/protocol-ai.mdx | New AI Protocol page for agents, RAG pipelines, NLQ, and predictive models, including AI.* configuration examples. |
| content/docs/concepts/meta.json | Extends the English concepts navigation metadata with a “Protocol Namespaces” group linking to each new protocol-* concept page. |
| content/docs/concepts/meta.cn.json | Mirrors the navigation update in Chinese, adding the 协议命名空间 group with the same protocol pages. |
| content/docs/concepts/enterprise-patterns.mdx | Adjusts references in the enterprise patterns doc to point to Automation/Data protocols instead of ObjectOS/ObjectQL and keeps examples conceptually aligned with the new architecture. |
| content/docs/concepts/enterprise-patterns.cn.mdx | Chinese enterprise patterns doc updated to refer to 自动化协议/数据协议 in line with the new terminology. |
| content/docs/concepts/architecture.mdx | Rewrites the architecture doc around 11 protocol namespaces, grouping them into Data/Control/View layers and adding a protocol dependency graph and updated request lifecycle walkthrough. |
| content/docs/concepts/architecture.cn.mdx | Chinese architecture doc updated in sync with the English version to describe the protocol-based, three-layer architecture and dependencies. |
</details>

The `System.Event`, `System.EventHandler`, `System.EventRoute`, and `System.Job` examples here don’t match the actual System protocol types: for example, `Event` in `events.zod.ts` has no `namespace` or `correlationId` fields, `EventHandler` is a function-based schema (not an object with `action`/`filter`), `EventRoute` uses `from`/`to` strings rather than `source`/`destinations`, and `JobSchema` requires an `id`, a `handler` function, and schedule shapes like `intervalMs` and `at` instead of `interval`/`unit` plus an `action` object. This divergence means these code samples won’t type‑check against `@objectstack/spec` and could mislead implementers; please either update them to reflect the real schemas or clearly indicate that they are high-level conceptual shapes rather than exact `System.*` types.

"visualizeable" is misspelled here; the standard spelling is "visualizable". Since this sentence was modified in this PR, it’s a good opportunity to correct the spelling in the updated text.
```suggestion
We define the lifecycle as a **Finite State Machine (FSM)** in the Automation Protocol (Workflow). This makes the business process deterministic and visualizable.
```

This query example uses `Data.Query` with `filters` and `sort` properties, but the Data protocol currently exports `QueryAST`/`QueryInput` types with a `where` field for filters and `orderBy` for sorting. As a result, this code won’t align with the actual `QuerySchema` and will confuse developers trying to copy-paste it; consider updating the example to use the real field names and exported query types, or clearly mark it as pseudo-code rather than a concrete type-safe example.

`const capabilities: Driver.DriverCapabilities` is shown with `queryFilters` and `queryAggregations` as string arrays and additional flags like `queryJoins`, but the actual `DriverCapabilities` schema in `driver.zod.ts` defines these as boolean capabilities (e.g. `queryFilters: boolean`, `queryAggregations: boolean`, `joins: boolean`, etc.). This mismatch means the example won’t type-check against `@objectstack/spec` and misrepresents how capabilities are declared; it would be better to align the shape with the real schema or explicitly label this as conceptual rather than a concrete `Driver.DriverCapabilities` instance.

The custom driver example imports `Query` from `"@objectstack/spec/driver"` and uses it in the `find` method signature, but the driver subpath does not export a `Query` type (query types live under the Data protocol as `QueryAST`/`QueryInput`). This will not compile as written; consider either importing the correct Data query type (e.g. from `@objectstack/spec/data`) or changing the example to use the exported `DriverInterface` type parameterized over the existing query AST type.

These snippets reference `Kernel.Manifest`, `Kernel.Plugin`, and `Kernel.PluginContext`, but the Kernel namespace currently exports `ManifestSchema`/`ObjectStackManifest`, `PluginDefinition`, and `PluginContextData` instead, so these type names don’t exist in `@objectstack/spec`. To avoid confusing users and breaking copy‑pasted examples, please either adjust the docs to use the actual exported types or add matching type aliases in the Kernel module so the documented names are real.

The `Auth.PasswordPolicy`, `Auth.SessionPolicy`, and `Auth.NetworkPolicy` types used in these examples are not exported by `@objectstack/spec`; only the underlying schemas (`PasswordPolicySchema`, `SessionPolicySchema`, `NetworkPolicySchema`) are available via `auth/policy.zod.ts`. In addition, the property names and semantics here (e.g. `requireSpecialChars`, `preventReuse`, `maxAge`, `maxDuration`, `allowedIpRanges`) don’t line up with the actual schema fields (`requireSymbols`, `historyCount`, `expirationDays`, `idleTimeout`/`absoluteTimeout`, `trustedRanges`, etc.), so these objects won’t type‑check; it would be clearer either to mirror the real schema shapes or to introduce properly named exported types that match the documented structure.

This Object Permission and FLS documentation shows `Permission.ObjectPermission` and `Permission.FieldPermission` as including `object`/`field` identifiers and uses an `OWDModel` object with `internalAccess`/`externalAccess` and values like `read_only`/`read_write`, but in the spec the `ObjectPermission` and `FieldPermission` types are bare permission bitsets (no object/field keys), `OWDModel` is an enum of strings, and the allowed OWD values are `private`/`public_read`/`public_read_write`/`controlled_by_parent`. As written, these examples don’t reflect the actual schemas in `permission.zod.ts` and `sharing.zod.ts` and won’t type‑check, so it would be good to either update the examples to match the current types or add new exported types that match the documented structures.

The example types `Data.Object` and the `labelPlural` property do not match the current Data protocol types: `@objectstack/spec` exports `ServiceObject` (via `ObjectSchema`) with a `pluralLabel` property instead. As written, this snippet will not type-check against the library; either update the example to use the actual exported type and property names (e.g. `ServiceObject` / `pluralLabel`) or add the corresponding aliases in the spec to match the documented API.
```suggestion
import type { ServiceObject } from '@objectstack/spec';

const accountObject: ServiceObject = {
  name: 'account',
  label: 'Account',
  pluralLabel: 'Accounts',
```

The `UI.ListView` example here introduces properties like `object`, `label`, `pageSize`, `actions`, and nested column configs with `width`/`format`, but the actual `ListView` schema in `view.zod.ts` uses a different shape (data source via `data`, `columns` as strings or `ListColumn` objects, `pagination` as a nested config, and no `actions` field). As a result, this snippet will not type‑check against `UI.ListView` and gives an inaccurate picture of the current protocol; consider updating it to mirror the real `ListViewSchema` fields or explicitly call out that this is a higher‑level conceptual API rather than the concrete spec type.

This `Automation.WorkflowRule` example uses `object` and a nested `condition.formula` field, but the actual `WorkflowRule` type in `automation/workflow.zod.ts` expects `objectName` and a `criteria: string` formula field, along with options like `timeTriggers` and `reevaluateOnChange`. Because of this, the documented shape will not type‑check against `Automation.WorkflowRule` and may confuse users; it would be better to align the property names and structure with the existing schema or clearly mark this as conceptual pseudo‑code instead of a concrete type example.
